Edit: For Steam Deck owners...I tried this on the deck and it ran with no issues. I only put 20 mins into it on the Deck in desktop mode, doing the training.Graphics had to be dropped to normal for it to run smooth. But no proton forcing or launch option changes needed. 

Now on to the review:

Ok before I start talking about the actual game of Zombie Girl. I think i need to discuss how it actually entered my collection. I am not a adult game player. Actually nudity and sex in games is uncomfortable to me. its not that I am prude...its just....weird watching game characters do it. But I am not foreign to it....I mean I did Killer 7 and loved it, and I am actually one of the few who have played Duke Nukem Forever. But i just want to state where I come from.

Now the bizarre history of this game and myself. The first time I saw it was about a month ago while looking up new indie games coming soon. This was on the list, and I saw the title, and though it would be a Silent Hill type game maybe. It was the first one I clicked on the list on the indie site I found too. And...imagine my surprise when i saw the shots with the blurs....and the nudity and sex warning. So..I closed it and moved on.

The next time I saw it was on another site of indie games. That picture of the tongue sticking out made me laugh knowing it is a adult game. I mean still at this point it looks...weird.

Fast forward to last night...and it shows up again on my suggested games list. Really this one?

Then today I wake up and it is in my google feed with someone reviewing it. So now I figure i would look at it and was surprised what the game really was. 

I then came here and started reading the reviews: all the ones disappointed about there being no boobies and such. Knowing that, and being on sale for $4.19....its worth the experiment.

I have to say...this game, for what it is and what it is priced, is actually worth it. its not going to win awards for greatest game ever...but it is still pretty fun.

A few things I didn't like: even on my computer, which is fairly high end (I mean it is not Intelligence Agency class...but it was custom built recently), the game runs a bit choppy. It isn't too bad...but it is noticeable, and can make movement and aim a bit rough. Also the recoil is a bit annoying how it works. It feels like some well aimed shots can miss now and then.

The clothing coming off feature annoyed me back on 3rd Birthday. it felt like a cheap way to sell the game. But it doesn't bother me in this...in fact I barely even notice it. I am too focused on gunning down my foes....which is surprising pretty hard core. Its no anime style action, even though the main character looks it.

I know I have only gotten like 45 mins of playtime so far...but for $4.19 that ain't bad. I am sure I will get more. And a movie is usually just twice as long, but the cost of a movie ticket is usually anywhere from $10 - $18. You do the math if $4.19 is worth 45 mins.

I did..and that is why I actually thumbs up this one.

Edit: I lowered the graphic level and everything does play smoothly. Much better now.

Alright, another game that triggers entitled Gamers, who are ok with $60+ gambling simulators... But are butt hurt about a $7 game (discounted on launch date, mind you) for not being polished and 100% perfect on day one. 

"B-b-b-but, there is no sex or nudity!" Game literally does not say that is has sex or nudity in it, if you read the description of the games you buy, before buying them. Reading is FUN!

Alright, I could rant all day about the low level mentality of negative reviewers, but let's actually break stuff down here. 

Obviously, the game hasn't even been out for a few days, so it has some issues. Dev team seems responsive and looks to be making fixes, which is a great sign. 

This "review" is more so along the lines of "first impressions" rather than a full review. I'll explain why later. 

I came across this game's page just pure randomly, about a week before it came out, so I had no clue it was even being made. I saw the video of game-play and first thing I thought was "whoa, I get THAT for $7?!" Awesome camera moment, cool looking design, sexy lady, excellent graphics. I was sold. 

Level designs are a hit or miss, giving that they are randomly generated. They merge well together, but you will see the same room assets used over and over. Some levels it fits in with the themes and can be overlooked, but when you are lost in a level, forced to see the same walls for minutes on end, the blandness can start to show. Regardless, each level looks unique to the previous one, and looks great for what it is. The underground laboratory is my personal favorite. 

The camera movement is very dynamic, but if you focus on her jog camera "shake", it is slightly nauseating/irritating on the eyes. Still cooling looking and pumps up the action and game-play. 

That's really it for the positives, not because there isn't a lot of them, but mostly because it is a very simple, compacted game. Very A to Z, straight to the point. 

There are some issues I came across: 

Reviving only to fall through the levels endlessly. 

Enemies bodies stretching/warping apart at their torsos. 

Issues with enemy sound fx on maps with two floors. You will find out very soon that you will hear enemies, but not see anything in sight. That is because they are above you, and react to you being underneath them. Now in some cases, it can be played off that "something is happening on the floor above me" kinda situation, and it can add to the atmosphere... but when you start having to back track, you will notice how those sound fx are more and more out of place. In the Ruins, this becomes more flawed, as I get the feeling growling enemies are placed behind unreachable areas, just to trigger growling sounds to scare you... yeah, it works, but it comes off as cheap jump-scare tactics. 

Getting stuck and rag-dolling in the piped floors in the Underground Laboratory. 

Key puzzle items not spawning. Puzzle items spawning that you never need, since the levels are randomly generated, not all the puzzles are generated or are the same, each time. 

Not being able to find all/or any story files during a level. This means if you want to actually read what the game's story is about, you have to wait and collect all the files on multiple play-throughs, taking who knows how long. The files should be a guaranteed spawns, not random.

As I mention earlier, since I can't really experiences the full game, due to RNG story files spawning, I can't really fully review the game. Until I can beat the game and read all the files....

Speaking of beating the game....

Yeah, that ain't happening, the last boss needs HUGE NERFING. You are just simply not mobile enough to handle everything it is throwing at you. If anything, the last boss shows how useless you character really is. This needs to be fixed ASAP, even on easy, it is unbeatable. Not to mention you have to watch the cutscene intro every time you try again...

No good. 

But hey, for a little indie sexy horror game, it is pretty solid. Needs some fixing, but giving this is Utopia's first game, there is a lot of impressive stuff here for how small the package is. 

SIMPLE, yes, but very sleek and has potential. The game is $7, not $60, you will be ok if you don't like it. Go give money to your favorite THOT, and ask her to write your name on her arm, so that you can feel better. *pat pat* 

Seriously people...

Anyways, beyond the glitches and balance issues, my only real personal issue with the game, is the lack of character customization. Now Utopia has mentioned the Steam Workshop, for those who are crying about no nudity in the game...

My only issue with this, is that is sounds like they are going to send those who want character customization, to the Steam Workshop as well...

Now granted, this is a super small budgeted game, with a small price tag. So if Utopia can't add character customization directing into the game, I get it. But if anything, let us change the colors of her hair and clothes, at the very least.

But yeah, that's really it, tiny game, tiny first impressions review. Hopefully they fix everything, maybe add some farm-able achievements and more unlockables in the future. 

It's not prefect, but it stood out enough for me to enjoy it, compared to most mainstream garbage. I give it a mid-tier score, but would edit my review to raise it, if they make most the changes I suggested.

Overall: 6/10

Edit: Forgot to talk about the multi-floor sound fx issues.

*TLDR: 2/10 would wait, hopefully dev('s) figure out what sort of game they are trying to release to the public*

Great game so far. Definitely a new take on the genre. I am usually not into FPS style games but I thought I would give this one and a try and I am not disappointed. The only bug that I ran into that really bothers me is the view gets obstructed when backed up to a wall or when trying to pie off corners in a stairwell. For the price and the fact this is an intro game, I would feel comfortable giving it a 7/10. With some more time and development this could be a really nice game, toss in a mini-map and it could be worth $40 or more.

As of right now there are a bunch of things that need tweaking. overall gameplay balance. Restrictive movement when sprinting. AI ranging from complete idiots to instantly mowing you down from 100 metres away. Slow dodge roll when running. Audio balance. Generic looking enemies and environments. I could list a lot more.

However it does seem like the developer is actively updating the game. So while I wouldn't recommend it right now, there is a good chance that in the not so distant future i could change this to a thumbs up. Currently it's an aggressively mediocre game at it's best but that could change for the better in a few updates.

For my First Impressions of Zombie Girl check out my video here: https://youtu.be/bqZoPdZLwpc
